items.title: Airline Wi-Fi Has a Lie-Flat Seat Problem
items.summary: United has a real lead with Starlink and is smart to make as much noise about it as possible. Travel history suggests the lead won't last nearly as long as the enthusiasm around it.

items.title: ‘The P&L Doesn’t Lie’: Hotels See More AI Costs Than Bottom-Line Gains
items.summary: Hotel tech investments keep climbing, but profits aren't keeping pace. Can hotels promise that AI will mean no job cuts and a payoff on the P&L at the same time?

items.title: No Starlink? United Airlines Targets Rivals With Status Match Offer
items.summary: United is betting that Starlink will become one of its biggest selling points as it ramps up rollout of the in-flight Wi-Fi. Meanwhile, its chief rival, Delta, is receiving pushback online for not choosing the internet provider.

items.title: Creator Backlash Hits Travel: From the U.S. Open to Cruise Ships
items.summary: Cruise lines and live events are giving influencers insider access to reach young audiences. Certain partnerships have sparked backlash from paying guests.

items.title: Strawberry’s Case for Fixing the Data Before the Model
items.summary: Strawberry's tech chief sees AI models commoditizing and the edge moving to clean, connected data. In Europe, she wants regulators judging rules by whether they work as much as by how well they are documented.

items.title: Leela Palaces’ CEO on the Overlooked Detail That Can Make (or Break) a Hotel Stay
items.summary: On this episode of Suite Success, host Katie Cline sits down with Anuraag Bhatnagar, CEO of The Leela Palaces, Hotels and Resorts, and explores his hospitality “calling,” hiring for values, and delivering luxury through deep human connection and anticipatory service rather than t

items.title: Ras Al Khaimah Hotels Renovate to Capture the ‘Wynn Effect’
items.summary: A single resort opening is reshaping how an entire destination's hotels renovate, price and package their rooms — well before its doors open.

items.title: Minor Hotels Wants a ‘Vietnam Network,’ Not Just Beach Resorts
items.summary: Minor Hotels built its Vietnam business around overseas travelers heading to the beach. Now rising domestic travel, corporate business and meetings are giving the hotel group a reason to move into Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City.
